title: A Summer for the Garden Again
premise: Lior Vane inherited Vane Hollow vineyard along with its crushing debts, and the only way to save it is a co-ownership clause that unexpectedly names her estranged childhood friend, Juniper Ashe, on the deed. Forced to share one stubborn orchard through a single make-or-break harvest season, the two women rebuild trust while creditors circle and the town bets on their failure. When Juniper is offered a prestigious post abroad timed to the last train before harvest, Lior must finally choose love over the pride that ruined her family. They keep the vineyard together, and for the first time, Lior lets someone stay.
about_author: Sable Thackeray is the pen name of a former agricultural journalist who spent three seasons working small-family vineyards across the Pacific Northwest. She writes slow-burn romances about land, legacy, and the people who refuse to leave either behind.

chapters.title: The Deed with Two Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Buried under debt notices, Lior discovers the orchard deed legally requires co-owner Juniper Ashe — the friend who vanished twelve years ago after a betrayal Lior never explained. The emotional beat is dread: help arriving in the shape of the last person she wants.

chapters.title: Last Train, First Frost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper arrives intending to sign away her share and leave by Friday's train, but a surprise frost forces both women into an all-night salvage of the budding vines. Working shoulder to shoulder cracks old resentment; she misses the train without admitting why.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A creditor demands full repayment by harvest or foreclosure, and Lior hides the deadline from Juniper to protect her from the mess. The beat is guilt deepening as Juniper's practical brilliance starts saving money Lior didn't know could be saved.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Clearing dead trees, Juniper finds a childhood time capsule containing an unsent letter from young Lior explaining the betrayal was to protect her. Shaken, she confronts Lior, who deflects; the beat is longing sharpened by unfinished grief.

chapters.title: Tasting Notes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A town festival forces them to present the vineyard publicly as partners; a stolen moment in the cellar becomes a first kiss interrupted by the creditor's lawyer. The beat is hope ignited and immediately threatened.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper receives the overseas appointment she'd applied to months ago — starting the week before harvest, on the same day as the final train. She hides it, mirroring Lior's secrecy, and the beat is the corrosive symmetry of two protective lies.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A hailstorm wrecks half the crop days before picking; discovering Juniper's hidden offer at the worst moment, Lior lashes out that everyone leaves. Juniper, hurt, packs. The beat is the midpoint wound: love weaponized into accusation.

chapters.title: Rootstock
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the station, Juniper reads Lior's old unsent letter fully and understands the sacrifice beneath the silence. She chooses to stay off the train unilaterally, then must win back a proud woman who believes she's unworthy of staying.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Both POVs interwoven. With pickers short and the bank's inspector arriving at dawn, the whole town — moved by Juniper's quiet organizing — shows up to bring in the grapes overnight. Lior, exhausted, finally says the truth aloud: she'd rather lose everything than lose Juniper again.

chapters.title: A Summer for the Garden Again
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The harvest clears enough debt to restructure, and Juniper defers the post a year — then chooses not to take it at all. In spring they plant new rootstock together, both names on the deed and both meaning it. The beat is earned homecoming: second chances kept, not just given.
